issues.message: The roof does not reach past the walls on any two opposite sides: give it one block of overhang.

visual.summary: Lumber camp level 1: a small lean-to work shed with a lifting frame; still hard to tell it is a saw mill.
problems: Carlton asked for "a saw mill style instead of this puny thing": it is still a small lean-to shed that is hard to read. Make the saw the centrepiece: a long open mill hall with the saw bench in the middle, a log yard of stacked logs on one side and a plank stack on the other.
The roof is a single slope of one plank colour, flush with the walls: a proper gable or a lean-to with dark eaves and one block of overhang.
Everything is the same brown: add a cobblestone base under the posts and a dark frame against lighter infill.
Level 3 only adds a sapling and leaves over level 2: give it its own feature (a log cart, a second saw, a covered log store).

issues.message: 360 blocks, over the common budget of 350 (docs/STRUCTURES.md). A warning only.
The roof does not reach past the walls on any two opposite sides: give it one block of overhang.

visual.summary: Lumber camp level 1: now a long open saw-mill hall with a dark-eaved gable roof, a saw bench, a lifting crane, a log yard and plank stacks; reads as a saw mill.
problems: Almost everything is brown wood; a cobblestone base under the posts all round would ground it.
Level 3 adds only more stacks and saplings over level 2; a covered log store or a log cart would make it its own.
